results.summary: Landmark RCT demonstrating that adding temozolomide to radiotherapy improved median overall survival from 12.1 to 14.6 months and 2-year survival from 10% to 27% in newly diagnosed glioblastoma. This protocol remains the standard of care.
results.title: Radiotherapy plus concomitant and adjuvant temozolomide for glioblastoma

results.authors: Louis DN, Perry A, Wesseling P, et al.
results.summary: WHO 2021 integrates histological and molecular parameters for CNS tumor classification. Glioblastoma is now restricted to IDH-wildtype astrocytoma with necrosis, microvascular proliferation, or TERT promoter mutation/EGFR amplification/+7/-10; definitive classification requires tissue with molecular profiling. IDH mutation status is the primary determinant distinguishing GBM (IDH-wildtype) from lower-grade IDH-mutant gliomas.

patient.history_present_illness: Ms. Mei-Ling Chen is a 67-year-old right-handed retired mathematics teacher with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia who presents for inpatient evaluation after referral from an ophthalmologist. Approximately three weeks ago she began noticing that she was missing objects on her right side — bumping into doorframes, failing to notice food on the right side of her plate, and once nearly stepping into traffic from the right. She initially attributed these symptoms to her prior right eye cataract surgery and sought evaluation by her ophthalmologist. A formal visual field test performed two days prior to admission confirmed a dense right homonymous hemianopia. The ophthalmologist, recognizing this as a field loss in both eyes respecting the vertical meridian, immediately ordered brain imaging. An urgent outpatient MRI revealed a left occipital mass with surrounding edema, prompting same-day inpatient admission. On further questioning, the patient reports a four-week history of progressive occipital headaches that are worse in the early morning and have occasionally awakened her from sleep. She treated these initially with over-the-counter acetaminophen with partial relief, and noted they are unlike her prior tension headaches in both location and severity. Her husband corroborates the visual complaints and notes she has been unusually cautious while walking due to the visual loss. She denies nausea, vomiting, weakness, sensory loss, speech difficulty, seizures, or loss of consciousness. She has had no prior cancer diagnoses and no known carcinogen exposures. She lost approximately 2 kg over the past month, which she attributes to reduced appetite in the setting of her headaches. She was admitted directly from the ophthalmology clinic for further workup and neurosurgical evaluation.
